---
title: "How ToFScope works"
mermaid:
  theme: neutral
---

ToFScope analyzes ToF-SIMS acquisitions through a browser interface. This guide follows data through the major parts of the application and explains how the application is built.

An **acquisition** is an HDF5 (`.h5`) file containing measurements from an instrument. A **signal** describes the ion data being viewed; it can come from a stored channel or a custom mass window. An **analysis** is the current set of signals, selections, calibration, and display settings for an open file.

## The whole system

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Person[Person] -->|selects and explores| Browser[Browser interface]
    Browser <-->|requests and results| Service[ToFScope Python service]
    Service -->|reads| Source[Acquisition HDF5 files]
    Service -->|creates| Saved[Prepared or saved HDF5 copies]
    Service -->|provides data for| Export[Downloads and exports]
    Browser -->|renders| Views[Plots and 3D views]
```

In the usual local setup, the Python service and browser run on the same computer. The service also supplies the browser's application files; no JavaScript development environment (Node) is needed to run the packaged app. The browser displays results and communicates with the Python service, which runs the calculations. The service reads acquisitions, coordinates calculations, and can create separate copies or exports. It keeps the original acquisition unchanged.

ToFScope can also be configured for other deployments. Self-hosted use is under development, and the container workflow is untested. The [deployment guide](41-deployment.qmd) describes the current boundaries and setup.

## From acquisition to analysis

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Start[Start ToFScope and open it in a browser] --> Pick[Choose an acquisition or saved file]
    Pick --> Check{Needs preparation?}
    Check -->|Yes| Prepare[Preview and confirm a prepared copy]
    Prepare --> Explore
    Check -->|No| Explore[Explore signals and linked views]
    Explore --> Adjust[Choose regions, frames, and signals]
    Adjust --> Explore
    Explore --> More[Optional: calibrate depth, identify ions, or view in 3D]
    More --> Explore
    Explore --> Output[Export results or save an analysis copy]
    Output --> Reopen[Reopen a saved copy later]
```

Some acquisition files need initial ion maps created from raw measurement events before they can be explored. ToFScope previews that operation and creates a copy after the user confirms the action. In the *Explore* view, an ion image, mass spectrum, front projection, and depth profile provide different perspectives on the same acquisition. A user can select a region of interest, change the depth frame range, or compare signals; the views update to reflect those choices.

*Depth calibration* relates acquisition frames to physical depth when those depths are known. *Identify peak* helps compare measured peaks with isotope candidates. The *3D volume* view shows spatial signal data. The [user guide](../getting-started/index.qmd) provides instructions and limitations.

## Inside the application

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    subgraph Frontend[Browser interface]
        Screens[File picker, Explore, calibration, identification, 3D]
        Plots[Plot and 3D renderers]
        Client[API client and command queue]
        Screens --> Client
        Screens --> Plots
    end
    subgraph Backend[Python service]
        API[FastAPI: requests, sessions, validation]
        App[Application: analyses, commands, jobs, cache]
        Present[Presentation: display data and exports]
        Science[Science: integration, calibration, isotopes]
        Storage[Storage: HDF5 reading, preparation, copies]
        API --> App
        API --> Present
        App --> Science
        App --> Storage
        Present --> App
        Present --> Storage
        Storage --> Science
    end
    Client <-->|HTTP API| API
    Storage <--> Files[HDF5 files]
```

The **frontend** is the interface in the browser. It manages screens and interactions, sends requests, and draws plots and 3D scenes using data returned by the service. The **API** handles requests and session access between the browser and service. The application layer manages open analyses, commands, background jobs, and cached arrays. Presentation code prepares data for displays and exports, science code implements calculations, and storage code works with acquisition and saved files. Arrows show major relationships, not every dependency.

Readers who want to follow the code can start with [frontend screens](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/frontend/src/app), [frontend API code](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/frontend/src/api), and the backend's [API](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/src/tofscope/api), [application](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/src/tofscope/application), [presentation](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/src/tofscope/presentation), [science](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/src/tofscope/science), and [storage](https://github.com/datasophos/ToFScope/tree/main/src/tofscope/storage) directories.

## Following a selection

This example follows a change to an Explore selection, such as the region of interest. It shows the common path; individual actions can use different endpoints.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    actor Person
    participant UI as Browser
    participant API as Service API
    participant Analysis as Analysis state
    participant Data as View data
    Person->>UI: Change a selection
    UI->>API: Send an analysis command
    API->>Analysis: Validate and update the analysis
    Analysis-->>UI: Updated snapshot
    UI->>API: Request affected display panels
    API->>Data: Prepare panel data
    Data->>Data: Read or reuse arrays
    Data->>Data: Calculate views
    Data-->>UI: Panel data and revision
    UI->>UI: Check revision and redraw
```

An analysis snapshot describes the current choices and has a revision number. The browser uses it to decide which panels need fresh data and avoids displaying a response for an older revision. The service may reuse arrays from a memory cache to avoid repeated work; the cache is bounded and is not permanent storage.

Some operations take longer and use a background job instead of this immediate display path. Examples include custom signal integration, raw preparation, isotope measurements, and saving. The interface can report job progress and results while the service schedules the work.

## Data, saving, and exports

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Original[Original acquisition] -->|read| Session[Open analysis in service memory]
    Original -->|optional preparation creates| Prepared[Prepared HDF5 copy]
    Prepared -->|open| Session
    Session -->|Save as| Copy[Saved HDF5 analysis copy]
    Original -->|acquisition data copied into| Copy
    Copy -->|reopen| Session
    Session -->|export| Results[CSV or other downloadable results]
    Session -->|browser plot export| Image[PNG image]
```

The open analysis and in-progress jobs live in the service's memory; unsaved work is lost when it restarts. **Save as** creates a new HDF5 copy with the acquisition and committed analysis, so it can be reopened later. If the opened file is itself a prepared or saved copy, that file is the source for the new copy. CSV and image exports can be used to share results; **Save as** preserves the analysis for further work. [Configuration and storage](41-deployment.qmd#configuration-and-storage) covers space and filesystem requirements.

## From source code to a running app

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    TS[React and TypeScript source] -->|Node and Vite build| Assets[Built browser assets]
    Assets -->|copied into| Static[Python package static directory]
    Python[Python service source] --> Package[Python distribution]
    Static --> Package
    Package -->|install and run| Server[Local Python service]
    Server -->|serves assets and API| Browser[Browser]
```

Developers use Node to build the frontend. The build script copies the resulting files into `src/tofscope/static/`, where they are included in the Python distribution alongside the service. At runtime, the local service serves those prebuilt assets and the API; the browser runs the interface. The [building and testing instructions](40-building-and-testing.qmd) list the commands, and [deployment](41-deployment.qmd) describes other configurations.
